verdict.rationale: Semgrep ships an official, documented CLI. It installs via pipx or uv, runs `semgrep scan` and `semgrep ci`, and supports machine-readable SARIF export, `--dry-run`, `--autofix` and scanning without logging in. Community users corroborate scripting it, including feeding its SARIF output into LLM-driven triage. Missing for 10: explicit agent-oriented CLI documentation (e.g., guidance for AI agents invoking the CLI or a JSON output mode framed for agentic use), and independent confirmation that the cited Windows install problem is resolved.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can use an official CLI

citations.quote: You can run local Semgrep CLI scans with the Semgrep command-line tool.
semgrep scan - This is the recommended command for scanning local codebases or scanning a project when you don't have a Semgrep account
Built a tool using Semgrep's SARIF output plus prompted LLMs to help prioritize triage
